business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Lohia Corp Limited manufactures machinery and equipment for technical textiles, focused on solutions for producing polypropylene (PP) and high-density polyethylene (HDPE) woven fabric and sacks ("Raffia"), and provides end-to-end 'concept to commissioning' solutions across the woven fabric production lifecycle. Its machines are sold to producers of woven fabric used in packaging (cement, fertilizer, chemicals, polymer, food grain, minerals) and non-packaging applications, supplied to around 100 countries through an exclusive global sales network. As of March 31, 2025, its manufacturing facilities had an installed capacity to produce 240 tapelines, 13,800 circular looms and 108,000 tape winders annually.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Lohia Trade Services Limited (formerly Lohia Corp Limited) — Demerged Company: Its technical textile machinery business undertaking, including investment in five subsidiaries, was demerged into the Company under the Scheme approved by NCLT Allahabad on April 16, 2024; appointed date April 1, 2024, effective date May 1, 2024.
- Leesona Corp — Subsidiary (USA): In 2019 the business and assets of Leesona Corp were acquired through LC Acquisition, Inc., a subsidiary of the Demerged Company, which was renamed Leesona Corp. after the acquisition; brought winding technology and machinery for high performance fibres.
- Sundarlam Industries Private Limited — Group entity incorporated following a 2021 acquisition: In 2021 the Demerged Company acquired the lamination/coating machines business for woven fabric from a company in Bengaluru and incorporated Sundarlam Industries Private Limited.
- J.J. Jenkins Inc — Business acquired in 2024 through Subsidiary Leesona Corp: Supplier of synthetic fibre and monofilament machinery in the United States; acquired to expand the specialty yarns and tapes portfolio for medical and defence applications.
- OMGM SAS — Shareholders' agreement counterparty (manufacturer in Italy): Company has commenced sale of extrusion lines for technical monofilaments and for production of straps and ropes pursuant to this agreement.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration capabilities reduce dependence on external supply of parts and components for machine manufacturing and support services and enable maintenance of quality control. The Company designs and manufactures inverters, customized machine controllers and motors along with other products for its circular weaving machine and winders, and operates its own surface mount technology manufacturing line for printed circuit board assembly and testing, so inverters, controllers and motors are made in-house for use either as original parts or spare parts. It has an in-house sheet metal fabrication shop catering to all sheet metal part requirements, 100 computer numerical control (CNC) machines that manufacture parts required in its machines, and a 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) from a global internal precision-equipment supplier for adherence to specifications. Electrical parts like inverters and printed circuit boards are also produced in-house using imported electric parts manufacturing equipment, aided by electrical assembly shops at each manufacturing facility where electrical panels are assembled. Other manufacturing steps are integrated through plating shops, moulding shops, assembly and testing shops and paint shops located within the manufacturing facilities, minimising dependence on external service providers. On the inbound side, raw materials, parts and components are sourced from suppliers on a purchase order basis, usually valid for one and two years, without formal long-term agreements; key externally sourced components include extrusion die, pump and screw, gear-box, bearings, electric motors and drives, and certain key components such as electrical motors, sensors, PLC systems, invertors and gear boxes are procured from limited suppliers in India, Europe, USA, China and Japan. Forward reach is through an exclusive global sales network: four sales offices in India (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Kolkata, New Delhi) plus a corporate office, five international offices (Brazil, Russia, Thailand, UAE, USA), warehouses in India, UAE and USA, stockists in eight countries, 17 exclusive sales agents, and service engineers stationed in 12 cities in India and in 12 countries overseas.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: The production and sale of technical textiles and consequently sales volumes may be affected by general economic or industry conditions, including seasonal trends in the agriculture sector, recessionary trends in the global and domestic economies and volatility in construction. The cyclical nature of the agriculture and construction industries, both globally and in India, impacts the demand for packaging of bulk commodities, which in turn affects demand for machinery and equipment for manufacturing technical textiles. In particular, the agricultural sector is inherently seasonal and is further impacted by factors including agricultural commodity prices, costs of fertilizers and adverse weather conditions. Similarly, the construction sector is prone to seasonality owing to factors such as the inconsistent real estate market and economic downturns that cease construction activity. No seasonality figures or quarterly split for the issuer's own revenue are disclosed in the routed text.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue to invest in research and development and in in-house capabilities to deliver evolving technologies
- Expand the specialty yarns and tapes portfolio for medical and defence applications (basis for the 2024 acquisition of the business of J.J. Jenkins Inc)
- Extend into extrusion lines for technical monofilaments with diversified applications such as textiles, agriculture and sports

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leader in India and among the leading manufacturers globally of woven raffia machinery in a growing market
- Diverse product portfolio, offering end-to-end solutions for the woven plastic ecosystem
- Long-standing relationships with a diverse, global customer base through an extensive global sales and distribution network
- Advanced manufacturing infrastructure with comprehensive backward integration, supported by an in-house training centre
- Technology-driven operations with a strong focus on innovation-led research and development, leading to products that cater to dynamic market requirements
- Skilled and experienced management team with committed employee base

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **The Company states it has developed in-house capabilities to deliver evolving technologies and will continue to invest in research and development.**
- **Expand the specialty yarns and tapes portfolio for medical and defence applications, following the 2024 acquisition of the business of J.J. Jenkins Inc through subsidiary Leesona Corp.**
- **Sell extrusion lines for technical monofilaments (applications including textiles, agriculture and sports) and for the production of straps and ropes, pursuant to a shareholders' agreement with OMGM SAS, Italy.**
- **The Offer is a pure Offer for Sale of up to 42,259,970 Equity Shares of face value ₹ 1 each by the Selling Shareholders; the Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer.**
